newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ship owners say U.S. sanctions unfair.
newsitem.headline: Japan ship owners say U.S. sanctions unfair.

text.p: Japanese ship owners said on Thursday that the U.S. decision to impose retaliatory surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports was unfair, and that the threat should be immediately withdrawn.

"The U.S. decision is highly improper, not only because there is a strong possibility that the measure could violate a U.S.-Japan treaty on commerce and navigation," Isao Shintani, chairman of the Japanese Ship Owners' Association said in a statement.
"But also because the sanctions aimed at resolving port problems are directed at three innocent Japanese shipping firms," it said.
"The sanctions, if imposed, will bring about grave economic damage to the three Japanese shipping firms and cannot be accepted," it said.
"The decision should be withdrawn immediately," it said.

The Federal Maritime Commission said on Wednesday it would impose $100,000 surcharges on vessels in response to what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports. The measures take effect on April 14.

The commission said the surcharge would be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.
"We are urging the Japanese government to swiftly take steps to improve port practices," the statement said.
"We request the Japanese government to make every effort to do away with the unfair sanctions," it said.
